s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home
Received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and premature ventricular complexes with short-coupling interval

shortlist.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation-related arrhythmias
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene

shortlist.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history not provided, but the condition is a possible cause of recurrent ventricular arrhythmias

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Normal cardiac function and structure, no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure, this condition can cause ventricular arrhythmias

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval, which is characteristic of CPVT. Additionally, the patient experienced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, which are also consistent with CPVT.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation
rejected.why: Lack of evidence for idiopathic VF, as the patient had a clear trigger for the arrhythmia

rejected.label: Long QT Syndrome
rejected.why: Normal QT intervals on ECG make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Normal cardiac function and structure on echocardiography, and no evidence of right ventricular dysfunction

rejected.label: Early Repolarization Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of J-point elevation on ECG, which is a characteristic feature of ER syndrome
